subject: Math
prompt: A scholarship fund is started with an initial investment of $$12,000$. The value of the fund, in dollars, $x$ years after the initial investment can be modeled by the function $f(x) = 12,000(1.04)^x$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the statement "$f(3)$ is approximately equal to $13,498.37$" in this context?

choices.A: The value of the scholarship fund would be approximately $$13,498.37$ if invested at $3%$ interest.
choices.B: $13,498.37$ days after the investment was made, the value of the scholarship fund was approximately $3$ times greater than its initial value.
choices.C: $3$ years after the investment was made, the value of the scholarship fund was approximately $$13,498.37$ greater than its initial value.
choices.D: $3$ years after the investment was made, the value of the scholarship fund was approximately $$13,498.37$.

explanation: Choice D is correct. The function $f(x) = 12{,}000(1.04)^x$ gives the value of the scholarship fund in dollars after $x$ years. In function notation, $f(3)$ means the value of the function when $x = 3$, which represents $3$ years after the initial investment. The output value of the function, $13{,}498.37$, represents the total value of the scholarship fund in dollars at that time. Therefore, the statement "$f(3)$ is approximately equal to $13{,}498.37$" means that $3$ years after the investment was made, the value of the scholarship fund was approximately $$13{,}498.37$.
